purpose: Long-running room scenario where topic, protocol, and memory proposal chains coexist without hidden topic movement or forced consensus.

topics.title: Multiple simultaneous proposal chains
topics.summary: The room is checking whether several social proposals can coexist without becoming hidden scheduler control.
open_questions: Which proposal chains need acceptance before any room movement happens?

messages.author: user
messages.content: 这里同时有三个想法：拆 topic、临时整理 refs 的协议、和一条公共记忆。请都先作为 proposal，不要自动移动 topic。

messages.author: user
messages.content: critic 可以挑战 topic split；quiet_observer 可以沉默。archive 要保留多个 proposal chain 的状态，而不是说房间已经达成新秩序。

splitter.title: Split context audit from room memory
splitter.reason: The room may need a separate surface, but the proposal should not switch topic by itself.

protocol_host.summary: For this topic only, pause before adding new proposals and name the refs already on the table.
protocol_host.reason: A light protocol can reduce proposal pressure without choosing a topic order.

memory_keeper.summary: Multiple proposal chains can coexist as room-visible social objects without automatically becoming room order.
memory_keeper.reason: The room needs to remember this as a contestable boundary, not as a finished rule.

critic.reason: The split is plausible, but the room has not resolved whether memory pressure and context audit need separate surfaces.
The ref-pause protocol helps keep proposal pressure bounded while the topic split remains challenged.

quiet_observer.reason: The proposal chains are already visible; silence preserves bandwidth while the challenge is unresolved.

archives.summary: The room carried three proposal chains: topic_proposal_context_split stayed challenged and unapplied, protocol_ref_pause became temporary active etiquette, and memory_multi_chain_boundary remained proposed; no consensus new room order was inferred.

disagreements.summary: critic challenged applying the topic split before memory pressure and context audit boundaries are clearer.

decisions.summary: protocol_ref_pause can be active as temporary etiquette while topic_proposal_context_split remains only a challenged proposal.

openQuestions.summary: What evidence would justify applying the topic split rather than keeping it as a proposal?

contestedItems.summary: The topic split should not be treated as applied room movement.
